qc/runs/hireops-live-desk-2026-10-02-r2/raw-evidence-index.json (whole file; five of its eleven artifact hashes recomputed)
evidence:
NESTING (static arithmetic, holds). task/task.toml:18 [agent].timeout_sec = 7200.0; :21 build_timeout_sec = 600.0; :27 [verifier].timeout_sec = 13200.0. task/tests/test.sh:213 `run_suite gates 1500`, :224 `run_suite scored 11100`, :207 `timeout "$budget_sec" rewardkit --max-concurrent-agent 1` (judges in a suite run one at a time, so the sum matters, not the max). Judge timeouts (judge.toml line 4 in each): gates/render 600, gates/constraints 600, scored/functional 9000, scored/polish 900, scored/visual 900. Each judge < its suite budget: 600 < 1500; 9000, 900, 900 < 11100. Sequential sums: gates 600+600 = 1200 < 1500 (300 s slack); scored 9000+900+900 = 10800 < 11100 (300 s slack). Budgets vs verifier: 1500 + 11100 = 12600 < 13200 (600 s slack). Sum of all judges 12000 < 13200 (internal-sheet wording). Liveness: test.sh:116-121 and :171-176 poll 120 x 0.25 s = 30 s at launch and after restart; restart_mcp.py helper timeout is the 55 s named in the contract, above the 30 s restart probe. Worst-case pre-suite overhead (30 s liveness plus copy/setup) fits inside the 600 s verifier slack. Verifier 13200 s = 3 h 40 min, below the five-hour limit. All values equal the frozen template and the reference figures in staged-task-contract.md:111 (gates 1500, scored 11100, verifier 13200): task/tests/test.sh is byte-identical to the template (sha256 bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa for both); task.toml differs from the template only in identity/metadata lines 5-15; all five judge timeouts equal the template's. No timeout was changed, so no authorization record is needed. Build: environment/Dockerfile is node:22-bookworm-slim plus apt (git, procps, sqlite3) and two global npm packages (express, better-sqlite3); 600 s is plausible for a cold build but was not timed in this round. Agent: 7200 s is the canonical value; no target-builder run exists to show it suffices for this brief (golden is about 3100 source lines).

SUFFICIENCY (unmeasured, the reason this is not a Pass). scored/functional/judge.toml holds 152 criteria (107271 bytes) with a 34962-byte prompt, graded by ONE batched judge call capped at 9000 s; the template's functional file holds 2 criteria with the same 9000 s. That is about 59 s of wall time per criterion, while the prompt prescribes 23 browser protocols (P1-P10, B1-B6, D1-D4, L1-L3) involving sign-ins as several roles, many fresh browser contexts, captured-request replays, Promise.all concurrency probes and one process restart, plus emitting 152 verdicts. Polish has 5 criteria in 900 s including multi-context live-update and session-resume flows. The raw evidence index states in its scope: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and target/Oracle scores are absent' and every entry is marked 'Not a configured judge run ... or judge-duration measurement'; the only duration figure in the indexed results is a single arrival_ms value in results/live-desk.json. preflight.json:246-248 itself labels timeout nesting as 'Arithmetic only, not measured workload fit'. I recomputed sha256 for live-desk.cjs, results/live-desk.json, results/server.log, regression/batch-domain-attempt2/results.json and regression/repair-coverage/results.json; all five match the index. The remaining six indexed artifacts (three PNGs, two .cjs drivers, none bearing on timing) were not re-hashed. Per the skill ('Never upgrade an unmeasured claim to Pass') and REVIEW_POLICY ('Workload is measured, not inferred from a timeout number'; 'Scripted Playwright duration is not LLM judge duration'), the 'long enough' half of this row cannot be attested. I ran no container and no judge.

CONSEQUENCE IF IT DOES NOT FIT. test.sh:207 wraps the suite in `timeout 11100`; test.sh:224-226 `if ! run_suite scored 11100; then exit 0`, leaving the reward at the zero record. A functional judge that exhausts 9000 s therefore scores a correct submission (including the golden) as 0 for a harness reason, which is the failure class the skill ranks highest. Hence P1 held as unmeasured rather than dropped.

WHAT IS GOOD. Nesting is correct with explicit slack at every level, sequential execution is accounted for, liveness and restart windows are consistent with the restart tool's timeout, and nothing drifts from the frozen template.
counterexample: Not demonstrated, so this is not a Fail. Plausible unexercised case: a fully conforming submission (the golden) is graded by the configured claude-code judge; working through 23 protocols for 152 functional criteria takes longer than 9000 s, rewardkit is cut off, run_suite returns non-zero at test.sh:224 and the run ends with the zero reward although the app is correct. Conversely a broken app that fails early gives the judge less to do and would finish in time, so a timeout would penalise good submissions more than bad ones. No run in this round confirms or refutes either.
suggested_fix: Run the full configured verifier once on the frozen golden and record per-judge wall time (gates render/constraints, functional, polish, visual) as hash-bound workload evidence. If functional finishes well inside 9000 s, this row can be re-reviewed as Pass with budgets unchanged. If it does not, either reduce redundant browser work and public scope together, or record a specific measured, authorized timeout change below five hours with the checker adapted narrowly; do not raise budgets without that measurement.
